question: Does the available Calapan River material support a species-level app batch, and what primary-source route remains?

sources.title: Fishes of Calapan River, City of Calapan, Oriental Mindoro, Philippines
sources.author: Bonifacio V. Labatos, Jr.
sources.publication: National Museum of the Philippines Journal of Natural History, volume 2, number 1 (2017), pages 1-10
sources.access: The ResearchGate record exposes the abstract and labels the author-uploaded full text as public, but its PDF endpoint returned 404 and the read-full-text endpoint returned 403 in this review. The National Museum library record identifies the 2017 print issue and lists five physical holdings; it does not provide a digitized article. Borrowing, scanning and reuse conditions were not established.

sources.title: Specialized Philippine Enterprise Reference of Experts and Scientists (SPHERES), Volume 2, Number 2
sources.author: Science and Technology Information Institute, Department of Science and Technology
sources.access: The official DOST bibliography lists a separate 2012, 60-page Fish Taxonomic Survey of Calapan River by Bonifacio V. Labatos, Jr., City of Calapan and BioNetwork Consultants. The report itself was not found or retrieved; its contents and relationship to the 2017 article remain unknown.

studyScope.waterbody: Calapan River, City of Calapan, Oriental Mindoro
studyScope.articleSamplingDurationAsReported: Three consecutive days; exact survey dates are not stated in the accessible abstract.
gearAsReported: bottom-set gill net in deeper portions

reportedResults.newIslandRecordsAsAbstractReports: One native and four introduced species; the accessible abstract does not name them.

limits: The 2017 abstract reports aggregate richness and categories but does not name taxa, show the taxon table, or link species to stations.
The 2017 publication year is not a confirmed field-sampling year; the abstract only says three consecutive days.
The five new island records are not identified in the accessible abstract and must not be guessed from the paper title or other Calapan studies.
The separate 2012 survey is a bibliographic lead only; do not merge its unreviewed contents with the 2017 article.
The ResearchGate record says author content may be subject to copyright. No item-specific open license or public-app reuse permission was verified.
Neither historical abstract establishes current presence, catchability, diet, local fishing rules or safety.

followUp.nextAction: Seek a legitimate article scan/access route and the separate 2012 survey through the National Museum and City of Calapan/BioNetwork bibliographic trail; in parallel, screen other MIMAROPA inland-water sources with accessible taxon-level evidence.
